andreas-von-bechtolsheim.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review under a limited search budget; not independently editorially reviewed; no rubric assigned (dimensions lacking evidence are stated in limitations)
andreas-von-bechtolsheim.summary: No evidence of political leverage, a preferential benefit linked to public power, or a wealth-power exchange was found. The one primary-source matter is a securities case: on 26 March 2024 the SEC alleged that Bechtolsheim, then Arista chair, learned of Cisco's planned Acacia acquisition on 8 July 2019 and traded Acacia options through accounts of a close relative and an associate, producing $415,726 in profits. He settled without admitting or denying, agreeing to a five-year officer/director bar and a $923,740 penalty. This is an enforcement action against him, not a political mechanism.
andreas-von-bechtolsheim.mechanism: No wealth-power mechanism established; securities enforcement matter only

support.text: SEC litigation release 25955 describes the complaint (N.D. Cal., 5:24-cv-01845), the alleged tips and trades, and the consent judgment terms subject to court approval. The relatives' accounts hold the trades; the allegation is against Bechtolsheim, and settlement involved no admission.

francois-pinault.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review under a limited search budget; not independently editorially reviewed; no rubric assigned (dimensions lacking evidence are stated in limitations)
francois-pinault.period: April 2019 pledge; Italian tax settlement May 2019 (covering 2011-2017)
francois-pinault.summary: No evidence of a political-power mechanism was found. Two documented items: a April 2019 pledge of EUR 100 million to Notre-Dame by the Pinault family through Artemis, and a May 2019 Kering settlement of EUR 1.25 billion with the Italian tax authority (EUR 897 million in additional tax plus penalties and interest) over Gucci in 2011-2017. The tax settlement is a state enforcement outcome against a company chaired by François-Henri Pinault, not a benefit; Kering did not admit wrongdoing.
francois-pinault.mechanism: No mechanism established; charitable pledge and a corporate tax settlement only

support.text: Kering agreed to pay EUR 897 million in additional tax, EUR 1.25 billion in total, to the Italian Revenue Agency over its Swiss subsidiary LGI and Gucci for 2011-2017; Kering said it was reached in a collaborative spirit and did not admit wrongdoing; Gucci executives were under criminal investigation as legal representatives. Concerns the group chaired by François-Henri Pinault, not François Pinault personally.
